Concatenate VCF files of the same samples into a gen_tibble

Source: R/gt_concat_vcfs.R
gt_concat_vcfs.Rd

This function reads several VCF files with the same samples but different loci (e.g. one file per chromosome, as distributed by many projects) into a single gen_tibble, as bcftools concat would, followed by gen_tibble(). It needs no space on disk beyond the gen_tibble: each file is read twice, once for its loci and samples, and once for its genotypes, which are written straight into the backing file of the gen_tibble. To combine files with different samples, use gt_merge_vcfs().

Usage

gt_concat_vcfs(
  files,
  backingfile = NULL,
  valid_alleles = c("A", "T", "C", "G"),
  missing_alleles = c("0", "."),
  allow_duplicates = FALSE,
  names_as_int = TRUE,
  chromosomes_as_int = FALSE,
  n_cores = 1,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

files

a character vector with the paths to two or more VCF files (.vcf or .vcf.gz, which are read faster if compressed with bgzip), in the order in which their loci should be in the gen_tibble.

backingfile

the path, including the file name without extension, for the backing files of the gen_tibble (a .bk file for the genotypes, a .rds file for the FBM, and a .gt file for the gen_tibble). If NULL, the path of the first file is used, with "_concat" added to its name (and a version number if those files already exist, as in gen_tibble()).

valid_alleles

a vector of valid allele values; it defaults to 'A','T', 'C' and 'G'.

missing_alleles

a vector of values in the VCF files that are considered as missing alleles ('.' is always missing).

allow_duplicates

boolean: whether to allow duplicated loci (the same chromosome and position) or duplicated loci names in the gen_tibble (see gen_tibble()).

names_as_int

boolean: whether the loci names are integers (the index of each locus in the gen_tibble) rather than the VCF IDs, which saves memory with many loci (see gen_tibble()). Note that it defaults to TRUE, unlike in gen_tibble() (where it defaults to FALSE): concatenating VCF files is mostly used for large datasets, in which the loci names take most of the memory of the gen_tibble and are rarely needed (loci are identified by their chromosome and position). Set it to FALSE to keep the VCF IDs. With integer names, the VCF IDs (with the chromosomes and positions) are written to a sidecar file next to the backing file, from which gt_lookup_loci() and gt_restore_loci() get them back.

chromosomes_as_int

boolean: whether the chromosomes are integer codes rather than a factor, which saves memory with many chromosomes (e.g. RAD loci assembled de novo); the names are written to a sidecar file next to the backing file (see gen_tibble() and gt_lookup_chromosomes()). Default is FALSE.

n_cores

the number of cores used to decompress bgzipped files and to parse the genotypes. Defaults to 1.

quiet

boolean: whether to omit the report of the concatenation.

Value

a gen_tibble with the data of all files (saved, as with gen_tibble()).

Details

As with gen_tibble(), only biallelic SNPs are read from each file. The loci of the gen_tibble are those of the first file, followed by those of the second file, and so on (as in bcftools concat), so the files should be given in the order of their chromosomes. The same chromosome can be split across several files (e.g. in chunks), but duplicated loci (the same chromosome and position) are an error, unless allow_duplicates = TRUE.

All files must have the same samples, but they can be in a different order in each file: the samples of the gen_tibble are in the order of the first file, and the genotypes of the other files are reordered to match. Sample names must be unique within each file.

As in gen_tibble(), the ploidy of each individual is estimated from the first variants of each file; the ploidy of an individual in the gen_tibble is its largest ploidy across files (e.g. with a file of the X chromosome in which males are haploid, males are still diploid). Files in which the genotypes of an individual are all missing in the first variants are ignored for its ploidy (unless they all are).

Unlike gen_tibble(), by default (names_as_int = TRUE) the loci are named with integers (their index in the gen_tibble), rather than with their VCF IDs, to save memory with large datasets. With names_as_int = FALSE, loci take their VCF IDs (a missing ID '.' gives a name made of the chromosome and the position, as in gen_tibble()).

See also

gt_merge_vcfs() to merge VCF files with different samples.

Examples

# two VCF files with the same individuals, one for each chromosome
example_gt <- load_example_gt("gen_tbl")
vcf_chr1 <- gt_as_vcf(select_loci(example_gt, 1:4),
  file = tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
)
vcf_chr2 <- gt_as_vcf(select_loci(example_gt, 5:6),
  file = tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
)
# concatenate them, keeping the VCF IDs as loci names (by default, unlike
# gen_tibble(), loci are named with integers to save memory)
concat_gt <- gt_concat_vcfs(c(vcf_chr1, vcf_chr2),
  names_as_int = FALSE,
  backingfile = tempfile("concat_")
)
#> reading the loci of /tmp/RtmpmlLt0o/file1f1d3b30f263.vcf
#> reading the loci of /tmp/RtmpmlLt0o/file1f1d4f0c57f0.vcf
#> concatenating 2 VCF files with 7 samples: 6 loci (biallelic SNPs)
#> reading the genotypes of /tmp/RtmpmlLt0o/file1f1d3b30f263.vcf
#> reading the genotypes of /tmp/RtmpmlLt0o/file1f1d4f0c57f0.vcf
#> 
#> gen_tibble saved to /tmp/RtmpmlLt0o/concat_1f1d76512bdd.gt
#> using FBM RDS: /tmp/RtmpmlLt0o/concat_1f1d76512bdd.rds
#> with FBM backing file: /tmp/RtmpmlLt0o/concat_1f1d76512bdd.bk
#> make sure that you do NOT delete those files!
#> to reload the gen_tibble in another session, use:
#> gt_load('/tmp/RtmpmlLt0o/concat_1f1d76512bdd.gt')
concat_gt
#> # A gen_tibble: 6 loci
#> # A tibble:     7 × 2
#>   id     genotypes
#>   <chr> <vctr_SNP>
#> 1 a      [1,1,...]
#> 2 b      [2,1,...]
#> 3 c      [2,.,...]
#> 4 d      [1,0,...]
#> 5 e      [1,2,...]
#> 6 f      [0,0,...]
#> 7 g      [0,1,...]
show_loci(concat_gt)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   big_index name  chromosome position genetic_dist allele_ref allele_alt
#>       <int> <chr> <fct>         <int>        <dbl> <chr>      <chr>     
#> 1         1 rs1   chr1              3            0 A          T         
#> 2         2 rs2   chr1              5            0 T          C
